A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Nested Slice Sampling work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–F are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original sampling experiments on synthetic targets, Inference Gym models and Gaussian-process regression, together with scaling, ablation and numerical theory-validation results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds adaptive-versus-fixed-schedule results in Table 4 and a JAXNS comparison in Table 11.

M1.justification: The core NSS procedure retains batched deletion/resampling, HRSS mutation, covariance whitening and the same reported defaults. Added pseudocode, tuning guidance and cap explanations do not establish a revised underlying sampler. Fixed-schedule replay is introduced as an experimental control.

E1.justification: New Appendix A.2 evaluates a Gaussian-prior/Gaussian-likelihood target and a six-component Gaussian mixture with strongly unequal mode masses, both in 20 dimensions. These extend synthetic test coverage; the existing synthetic, Inference Gym, GP and geometric test scenarios remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds AIS with an independent-MH kernel to the new overhead comparison in Table 4. It also adds JAXNS to the Mauna Loa comparison previously containing NSS and two UltraNest configurations (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 11). Existing comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces a controlled comparison of adaptive execution against replay of precomputed schedules using jax.lax.scan for NSS and SMC-IRMH, with 1000 particles and an AIS control using the same independent-MH kernel. The retained benchmarks' splits, budgets, metrics and numerical defaults are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2 tests the runtime overhead of adaptive execution and schedule discovery, while also examining reliability on an imbalanced mixture. Existing mutation-length, particle-count, batch-size, cost-variability and constrained-sampler analyses remain; moving their figures does not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: The five-seed reporting practice, ten-run evidence-scaling study and 100 volume-shrinkage simulations are retained. New Table 4 follows the existing five-run practice, and the additional uncertainty plot does not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports mixture log evidence of -72.49 ± 1.03 for NSS and -91.83 ± 0.38 for AIS, against analytic -73.68. Table 11 adds JAXNS at 2611 seconds versus the retained NSS result of 227 seconds. Table 3 adds derived ESS/s entries. Existing table values remain unchanged. The new Figure 2 uncertainty curve is not reconciled with Table 10: at k=900 it shows approximately 0.43, versus tabulated 0.47.

T1.justification: The formal results and proofs in Appendices D–F are retained. The effective-radius definition moves from v1 Equation 175 to v2 Equation 10, and existing theoretical remarks move into Section 3.3. Expanded intuition and discussion of existing assumptions do not constitute new theorems or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the central contributions. However, Sections 3.1–3.2 newly make explicit first/only claims for performant likelihood-synchronized parallelism and fully vectorized nested sampling, modestly strengthening the novelty claim.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the GP calibration interpretation: it removes the stronger calibration assertion from the figure caption and acknowledges absent ground-truth posteriors and possible simulation-based validation. It also explains when gradient-based alternatives are preferable, discusses failures of ellipsoidal approximations, and identifies plateau and nondeterministic-likelihood issues associated with shrinkage caps.

D1.justification: V2 adds details about synchronized likelihood calls, fixed-schedule execution, covariance-based width guidance and cap behavior. It documents JAXNS's sequential chains and 64-bit requirement. The expanded legacy-code comparison retains population and termination matching but drops v1's explicit equal-step-count assurance. Numerical defaults, hardware disclosure and the code-availability statement otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning around classical baselines for neural samplers, distinguishes evidence estimation from stacking/cross-validation, and discusses vectorized MCMC and specialized Hit-and-Run extensions. Related citations include Wu, Blessing, Dance, Paul and Modrák. These contextual additions retain the paper's central positioning around GPU-native nested sampling and tempered SMC.

P1.justification: Targeted restructuring separates optimal-width tuning into Section 3.3, revises background transitions and experimental interpretations, and adds Appendix A.2–A.3. Existing theoretical explanations are brought forward from Appendix E. The overall section structure and most text remain intact.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 9 is split between v2 Figures 2 and 11, with a new uncertainty panel; v1 Figure 10 becomes main-text Figure 3. V2 also adds Table 4 and two pseudocode boxes, expands Table 3 with ESS/s and the legacy comparison with a JAXNS row, and introduces publication headers. Other plotted results retain their original graphics.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens practical validation through the schedule-overhead experiment and JAXNS comparison, while making calibration claims and applicability limits more careful. Clearer tuning explanations and prominent scaling figures also improve accessibility. These are useful, targeted gains over v1's already substantial evidence; the unreconciled Figure 2/Table 10 uncertainties and incomplete mutation-setting detail in the expanded legacy comparison limit the improvement.
